mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week rebound in WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w, following a sharp decline, indicates a renewed return to office-based work. This will drive increased weekday footfall and spending in retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite the WORKPLACES rebound.

mechanism_narrative: A substantial week-on-week decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, combined with a strong rebound in TRANSIT, signals a shift in public behavior towards more out-of-home activities and commuting. This will directly boost RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 5 points week-on-week AND TRANSIT rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, or RESIDENTIAL mobility increases again while TRANSIT declines.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous strong rebound observed in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w indicates a broad-based return to pre-period routines, including commuting and associated activities. This synchronized increase will drive higher foot traffic to retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The positive correlation between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rebound and a subsequent RETAIL_REC increase fails to materialize over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of easing public health measures, the observed decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility from its recent peak, combined with a slight recovery in RETAIL_REC, suggests a shift from essential-only trips to more discretionary spending. This will lead to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase, or GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases again, indicating a return to essential-only trips.

mechanism_narrative: Despite a recent dip, the sustained elevated level of RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a continued preference for staying home or engaging in local activities. This persistent home-centric behavior will suppress overall RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5% change from baseline for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases significantly.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility continues its recent declining trend and falls below -20% from baseline, it will signal a general decrease in outdoor discretionary activity. This will negatively impact RETAIL_REC over the next week, as people reduce out-of-home leisure.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -15% within the next week, or RETAIL_REC increases in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of persistently low RETAIL_REC (below -30%) and a significant rebound in GROCERY_PHARM (above 0%) suggests a shift back towards essential-only outings and away from discretionary spending. This will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -30% while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable or declines over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a context of perceived easing of restrictions, a strong week-on-week rebound in TRANSIT mobility indicates increased public confidence in using shared transportation. This surge in transit usage will translate to higher RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: Despite the transit rebound, RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week, or even declines.
